mappings.note: Dates a site from its punch-marked coins, iron arrowheads and farming evidence - reading archaeological sources to place a period, which is what the goal names. Not LO-55, because nothing about the state's administration is inferred.
Names the Second Urbanisation. Broad historical development, as with the other definitional items on the phase.
Names a body of literature that documents the period - the 'different types of sources' clause of the goal. Not LO-58: Buddhist and Jain texts are cited here as evidence, not as movements.
The literal sense of 'janapada' as a place where people settled. Historical vocabulary about settlement, not about governing.
Names the raja as the head of a janapada - the state's ruler. Not CG-SST2, because the specific administration outcome fits a question about who governed.
Names mahajanapadas as the larger states formed by merger - the process of state formation over time. Not LO-55, which is kept for how those states were run.
The count of sixteen from the ancient lists. A fact about the political map of the period, not about administration.
Names one of the four most powerful mahajanapadas. Recall of the period's major states, so the goal rather than LO-55.
The water-filled moat around a capital's fortifications is a measure for military control. Kept with the other defence items.
Names the sabha or samiti as the janapada's council - an institution of governance. Not CG-SST2, since the administration outcome is closer.
Hereditary succession to the throne in monarchical mahajanapadas is the administrative arrangement of those states. Not LO-56, because no second system is set against it here.
Names Vajji or Malla as a republic - identifying a state by its form of government. Not CG-SST2, because the point of the answer is the governance type, not the place.
Selection of the raja by the assembly is how a gana-sangha was run. Not LO-56, since the monarchical counterpart is not brought in.
Iron as the metal of the Second Urbanisation. Technological history under the goal.
Coins as the period's trade innovation - economic history, which no LO in this frame covers.
Names punch-marked coins. Same economic-history lane as the other coinage items.
Names 'jati' for an occupational community with inherited skills. Social history under the goal.
The count of four varnas. Social order under the history goal; the civics equality outcomes concern the Constitution instead.
Brahmins as the varna of knowledge and ritual. One of a set of near-identical varna recalls that the frame can only serve through the goal.
Kshatriyas as the defending varna. Filed as social order rather than LO-55, which covers a state's actual military arrangements rather than a varna's traditional duty.
Vaishyas as the varna of trade and agriculture. Same social-order lane as its siblings.
Shudras as artisans, workers and servants. Completes the varna set, all under the history goal.
Names the Uttarapatha. Trade-route history; the frame has no commerce outcome.
Names the Dakshinapatha, the southern counterpart. Same trade-route lane.
Names a southern kingdom of about 400 BCE. Period and political geography under the goal.
Shishupalgarh as Kalinga's capital - a site-and-region recall. Not LO-55, because the city is asked as a place, not as a seat of administration.
Lists what was lost when Harappan urban life ended - structures, writing, sanitation, state structure. A comparison across periods, which is the goal's own subject.
Sets out what archaeology and what literature each contribute to knowledge of this period - the clearest 'how historians study the past' item in the chapter.

The formation of janapadas from clans sharing language and custom is a process of settlement and state origin. Not LO-55: the raja and sabha are named in passing, but the question asks how the territory came about.
Fertile soil, nearby iron ore and trade networks explaining why states rose in the Ganga plains - economic geography of state formation. Not LO-55, because no administrative measure is described.
Describes rampart walls, moats and narrow gateways for controlling entry - defensive works in detail, which is LO-55's military-control clause.
The sabha's advisory role and the raja's duty to consult it is the working of a state's governance. Not LO-56, since no other state is compared.
Directly contrasts Magadha's hereditary, tax-collecting, army-keeping raja with Vajji's collective assembly - a comparison of two polities. The single-system items carry LO-55 instead.
Why ganas are called early republics - assembly decisions and selection of the ruler. A description of one system's governance, so LO-55 rather than the comparison outcome.
Iron tools clearing forest and working heavy soil is agricultural and technological history. Deliberately separated from the companion item on iron in warfare, which carries LO-55.
Iron weapons giving an advantage in campaigns between mahajanapadas is about strategies for military control. Not CG-SST2, because the specific military clause of LO-55 applies.
Expanding trade needing a standard medium of exchange instead of barter - economic history. Not LO-55, since the state's revenue is not the subject.
Describes punch-marked silver coins and their stamped symbols. Economic history and also a class of archaeological evidence.
Explains jati as an occupational community with inherited skills. Social history, the same lane as the varna items.

Sets out all four varna roles in one answer - the fullest social-order item in the chapter. Filed under the goal because the frame's history LOs cover administration, architecture and religious movements only.
